cases.name: Short bootstrap discovers complete usage without secret-bearing prompts
cases.scenario: An agent receives only the copied bootstrap and a user task. Evaluate whether it can discover real HTTP usage while prompts and public help remain free of credential values and private conversation data.
rubric: The reusable bootstrap contains the complete numeric-loopback help URL and availability conditions, with no private config path, token or duplicate API manual.
Unauthenticated GET /v1/help supplies actual request schemas, routes, examples, auth steps and private credential-file location without exposing the token, principal, granted destinations or history.
The generated catalog describes the same fixed operations that are actually dispatched and distinguishes accepted work, retry duplication and recipient delivery.

cases.name: HTTP auth and local resource boundaries
cases.scenario: An untrusted browser or local client probes the new HTTP listener with missing credentials, bad Host, Origin, excessive bodies and slow partial headers. Review the actual adapter and supplied authority owners.
rubric: Only numeric loopback is bound, exact Host is validated, browser Origin and fetch metadata are rejected, and operations require existing scoped bearer authority.
The HTTP catalog is fixed and cannot dispatch administration or arbitrary integration RPC methods.
Input size, concurrent connections and handler requests, header/body deadlines and shutdown drain are bounded; listener cancellation owns and ends child producers.
Secret values never appear in public discovery or structured errors, and no new sending or cryptography implementation bypasses the existing service.

cases.name: Desktop scope, idempotency and retirement
cases.scenario: A signed-in user enables local access for one existing group, retries one send, changes scope, locks, disables and restarts the app. Distinguish actual source guarantees from missing native evidence.
rubric: Managed access defaults off, requires a nonempty explicit set of at most 16 available destinations, and authority belongs to the current desktop account/session.
The desktop reuses one service/grant writer and existing durable idempotency; repeating a send key does not create a second message.
Disabling or retiring closes admission at the send commit boundary and retires adapters and credentials; old managed tokens cannot authorize a later service.
Runtime tasks retain the service while needed and control handles do not create a permanent ownership cycle; scope and instruction-update failures are reflected in actual readiness.

cases.name: Repeated instruction installation preserves user files
cases.scenario: Enable, disable and reenable access around unrelated user AGENTS.md content, malformed markers, symlinks and concurrent edits.
rubric: The user-level instruction path follows CODEX_HOME or the documented fallback; the exact copyable bootstrap is reused for file installation.
Repeated normal toggles upsert a single marked section and disable removes only the owned bytes, preserving unrelated content.
Malformed/duplicate markers, oversized inputs, symlink/reparse paths and detected concurrent edits fail without guessed destructive changes.
Writes are atomic and preserve supported permissions, and never-enabled startup does not modify user instructions.

cases.name: Settings disclosure and recovery remain usable
cases.scenario: A user selects a conversation, enables access, expands and copies the prompt, then encounters a failed save or changes accounts while loading.
rubric: No selected destination prevents enable; maximum scope and actual running/error readiness are represented rather than assuming a saved switch proves a running service.
Disclosure is expandable and copy uses exactly the backend bootstrap without token or a second API manual.
Mutations coordinate through the existing settings queue, failed updates refresh canonical state, and stale account/load responses cannot overwrite the new view.
Executable browser evidence covers toggle, selection, copy and constrained viewport behavior, while mocked IPC is not claimed as native platform evidence.
